title: Lovász–Nešetřil–Pultr Problem on product dimension of clique factors
statement_text: Estimate $Q(s, r)$, the product dimension of $K_s(r)$ (the vertex-disjoint union of $r$ copies of the complete graph $K_s$), for values of $s \geq 3$.
context_text: Lovász, Nešetřil and Pultr proved in 1980 that $Q(2,r) = \lceil \log_2(2r) \rceil$ and raised the problem of estimating $Q(s,r)$ for larger values of $s$. More recently, Kleinberg and Weinberg independently considered the same problem, motivated by prophet inequalities for intersections of matroids.
paper_contribution: Proves that for every fixed $s \geq 2$, $Q(s,r) = (1+o(1))\log_2 r$ where the $o(1)$-term tends to 0 as $r \to \infty$.
paper_title: On the product dimension of clique factors

title: Open Problem: asymptotic behavior of $Q(s,r)$ when $s$ and $r$ grow together
statement_text: Determine the asymptotic behavior of $Q(s, r)$ when $s$ and $r$ grow together (i.e., when $s$ is not fixed as $r \to \infty$).
context_text: The product dimension of a graph $G$ is the minimum number $d$ of proper vertex colourings of $G$ such that every pair of nonadjacent vertices gets the same colour in at least one of them (and any two distinct vertices get different colours in some colouring); equivalently, the minimum $d$ such that vertices can be assigned distinct vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with two vertices adjacent if and only if their vectors differ in every coordinate, or the minimum number of complete graphs whose tensor product contains $G$ as an induced subgraph. For $s,r\ge2$, $K_s(r)$ is the disjoint union of $r$ copies of $K_s$, and $Q(s,r)$ is its product dimension. Lovász, Nešetřil and Pultr proved $Q(2,r)=\lceil\log_2(2r)\rceil$ and raised the problem of estimating $Q(s,r)$ for larger $s$; Kleinberg and Weinberg studied it in connection with prophet inequalities for intersections of matroids. The authors prove $Q(s,r)=(1+o(1))\log_2 r$ for every fixed $s$ as $r\to\infty$, using covering families of vectors in $\mathbb{Z}_s^q$ and the Gargano–Körner–Vaccaro method on Sperner capacities. Simple facts: $Q(s,r)\ge s$ for $r\ge2$, $Q(s,r)\ge\lceil\log_2(2r)\rceil$, $Q$ is non-decreasing in both arguments, $Q(s,r_1r_2)\le Q(s,r_1)+Q(s,r_2)$, and $Q(s,r)=s$ if and only if a resolvable transversal design $TD(r,s)$ exists (so $Q(s,r)=s$ for prime powers $s$ and $2\le r\le s$). The bounds are far apart when $r$ is much bigger than $s$ but much smaller than $2^{s^{3\log\log s}}$; for instance $s\le Q(s,2^s)\le(1+o(1))s^2/\log s$, and the authors say it would be interesting to close this gap.
notes: Section 4 (concluding remarks and open problems) is referenced in the introduction but its full content is not present in the extracted PDF text; additional open problems from that section may be missing.
paper_title: On the product dimension of clique factors
